sections.text:
The oil separator receive the effluents 
pumped from various points of the power plant.

The flow through the system will be by gravity. The 
influent head is at least 12" above the height of the CPS effluent weir. The influent 
enters the gravity separation section where heavy solids drop out. The flow then 
proceeds through polypropylene prefilter media before passing through the corrugated plate interceptor. 
Separated oil flows into the adjusted oil trough to out, the clean water flows 
over the effluent weir into a water sump, from which it can flow by gravity to 
the evaporation pond. If oil level exceed the limits specified, flow will be 
diverted back to the holding pond.

The influent 
overflows the inlet weir into a quiescent zone located ahead of the CPI pack. In this area 
the liquids velocities are slowed. The lighter gravity liquid rises to the 
peaks of the corrugations and continues to the rises until reaching the gutters 
at the inlet of the pack, and the heavier liquid flows out the lower portion of the 
pack to the effluent trough. If any 
solids are present, these solids collect in the valleys of the corrugations and 
are collected in gutters located at the pack outlet. These gutters direct 
the solids to the bottom of the separator basin.

Sludge 
buildup should be monitored closely, especially immediately after startup until 
experience is gained. Solids buildup should not be allowed to reach bottom of the CPI pack.

Sludge 
buildup should be monitored by observing 
the discharge from the sludge removal pump.

In removing 
sludge, short intervals of withdrawal are superior to one long withdrawal. The 
short intervals allow the sludge to resettle and therefore, help prevent 
"rat-holing".

Prior to 
draining it is necessary to remove the oil layer so as not to contaminate the 
effluent side of the basin.

Oil removal 
can be accomplished by lowering the bucket weir or by closing off the effluent so 
that the water level rises, forcing the oil layer into the oil bucket.

Maintenance 
Instructions for Corrugated Plate Separator

If the 
sludge level is properly maintained, no routine maintenance is required on the 
CPS, because there are no moving parts.

Supports 
systems such as oil withdrawal, sludge withdrawal, heaters or feed pump should 
be maintained in accordance with the instructions for those specific units.

Periodic 
visual inspection of the unit is recommended. This inspection should check for 
leaks, and determine whether the unit appears to be functioning properly, i.e. 
clean water flow over the effluent weir and oil over into the bucket weir.

Operating 
experience has shown that the smoothness of the corrugated plates generally 
prevents oils and solids from accumulating on their surfaces. If dirt and 
heavy oil do buildup within the pack or packs, they will require cleaning as 
this will reduce the efficiency of the unit.

The 
preferred method is to clean the packs in place. After the 
unit has been drained, a high pressure hose can be employed to wash down the 
plates. Prior to draining it is necessary, of course, to remove the oil layer. 
This is can accomplished by lowering the bucket weir height.

An alternative method is to remove the packs. Before attempting to lift the 
 pack, the units should be hosed down, the CPI structure won't support the 
 weight of heavy solids during lifting bar through the two lifting lugs.

When putting the unit back in service after draining, always fill with clean 
 water first.
Caution: Do not drain the separator until all of the oil has been removed.

Given below are problems which may be encountered, the possible causes, 
 and the recommended maintenance.
